# Proofread — results (generated by benchmarks/make_proofread_results.py)

Pre-registration: `docs/PROOFREAD_PREREG.md` (written before the confirmation run). 14 public datasets fixed in advance, seeds 701–705, 400-row tables, 70 runs, all reported.

## Headline

**Cells (H6):** TabPFN-3.5 beats the best of 7 baselines (chosen per dataset, after the fact) on **13/14 datasets**; mean precision@k gain +0.190 [+0.132, +0.240], one-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.00018 — supported.  
**Labels (H7):** TabPFN-3.5 beats the best of 4 baselines on **13/14**; mean AUROC gain +0.022 [+0.008, +0.041], p = 0.00085 — supported.

![hero](figures/proofread_hero.png)

## H6: cell errors (3% of cells corrupted; 5 error types)

Precision@k: of the k most suspicious cells (k = number of injected errors), the share that are real errors. The baseline column is the best of z-score, IsolationForest, ridge, kNN, random forest, HGB and HGB-quantile **for that dataset, chosen after seeing the results** (conservative). Fix error = mean |suggested − true value| in column SDs.

**Ablation (distribution vs point prediction):** the predictive-distribution score beats the residual of TabPFN's own point prediction on 14/14 datasets (mean precision@k 0.72 vs 0.54).

**Where it does not help:** climate-crashes is a table of independently sampled simulation parameters (no cross-column structure), so predicting a cell from the rest of its row cannot help and a per-column z-score wins (0.42 vs 0.34).

## Real data: raw Pima diabetes (OpenML 37)

Known issue: physiologically impossible zeros. Proofread flags the rare impossible zeros (BMI, glucose, blood pressure) and extreme values (skin fold 99 mm) among its top issues, and reports insulin/skin-fold zeros (49% / 30% of rows) as a column-level placeholder code rather than cell by cell. See `results/proofread_demos/pima_real.json`.


## Addendum (pre-registered: `docs/PROOFREAD_ADDENDUM_PREREG.md`)

Same 70 corrupted tables, regenerated from the seeds; Proofread's precision@k reproduced the confirmation exactly (max |difference| = 0.0).

### A1. Prior Labs' TabPFN outlier detector (tabpfn-extensions 0.6.3, `TabPFNUnsupervisedModel.outliers`, 10 permutations)

Row level ("does this row contain an error?", the detector's home turf): Proofread higher on **14/14** datasets, mean AUROC +0.264, one-sided Wilcoxon p = 6e-05. Cell level (row score broadcast): Proofread higher precision@k on 14/14.

| Dataset | Proofread precision@k | Outlier detector precision@k | Proofread row AUROC | Outlier detector row AUROC | Detector seconds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MagicTelescope | 0.73 | 0.04 | 0.925 | 0.569 | 45 |
| banknote | 0.74 | 0.25 | 0.966 | 0.803 | 18 |
| blood-transfusion | 0.78 | 0.10 | 0.972 | 0.473 | 16 |
| breast-cancer | 0.85 | 0.03 | 0.968 | 0.379 | 145 |
| climate-crashes | 0.34 | 0.03 | 0.693 | 0.436 | 91 |
| diabetes | 0.61 | 0.06 | 0.859 | 0.609 | 38 |
| eeg-eye-state | 0.83 | 0.12 | 0.966 | 0.920 | 71 |
| electricity | 0.71 | 0.12 | 0.936 | 0.649 | 31 |
| ilpd | 0.70 | 0.05 | 0.948 | 0.724 | 44 |
| kc1 | 0.87 | 0.03 | 0.983 | 0.727 | 96 |
| phoneme | 0.59 | 0.20 | 0.874 | 0.746 | 23 |
| spambase | 0.68 | 0.03 | 0.831 | 0.547 | 297 |
| steel-plates | 0.87 | 0.06 | 0.987 | 0.711 | 112 |
| wilt | 0.74 | 0.13 | 0.951 | 0.863 | 23 |

The detector was used as documented (fitted and scored on the same table, with a float64 compatibility shim; see the pre-registration amendment and `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`: the extension crashes on CUDA with tabpfn 9.x). Scoring in-sample may let a corrupted row partly explain itself, which could explain row AUROCs below 0.5 on three tables. It is a joint-density row detector, not designed to localise cells.

### A2. Operating point shown to users

| Threshold (−log₁₀ tail prob.) | Precision | Recall | Cells listed (70 tables) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 87.9% | 53.3% | 7110 |
| 3 | 94.8% | 19.0% | 2344 |

After this analysis the library/CLI default threshold was changed from 3 to 2 (a product setting, not a tested hypothesis).

## Pilots and abandoned directions (exploratory, development seeds; not evidence)

- Gradient of cross-validated loss w.r.t. soft labels as a label-error score: weak (AUROC 0.34–0.69 over 22 pilot runs); abandoned.
- Removing flagged label errors barely changes TabPFN accuracy (TabPFN-3.5 is robust to 10% uniform label noise).
- Full conformal prediction with TabPFN: set sizes similar to split conformal in a pilot; abandoned.
- Look-ahead (expected-error-reduction) active learning with TabPFN: not better than random/margin in a pilot; abandoned.

## Limitations

- Injected errors are synthetic (five realistic types); real-world error mixes differ. The Pima example is illustrative.
- Numeric continuous columns only (>10 distinct values); categorical-cell checks are future work.
- 400-row tables; each column costs 5 TabPFN fits (out-of-fold).
- A flag is a prompt to check the source, not proof of an error; surprise scores are not calibrated error probabilities.
